archetypes.name: shell-scope-ordering
archetypes.rationale: The plan sets module-level vars base_remote/base_ref at ~line 280+ but is_small_non_runtime_change is defined at ~line 79; any early-exit path that calls the function before the vars are set would silently use unbound variables.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read step-7a.sh and locate every call site of is_small_non_runtime_change relative to where the plan places the base_remote/base_ref assignments (after the argv and session-key resolution block, before the token-ledger.sh mark at line 334). Confirm there is no argument-validation or session-key-resolution early-exit path that invokes the function before those module-level variables are set, and note what bash produces for an unbound variable reference in that function body. Also verify that the plan's replacement of the inline BASE_ARGS=(--base-remote upstream --base-ref main) literal with derived vars does not silently affect any downstream consumer of BASE_ARGS other than the rebase-checkpoint-probe call the plan names. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: env-argv-doc-parity
archetypes.rationale: The plan's step-7a.md update claims LARCH_FORKED_TARGET=true is a trigger alongside --forked-target true, but the implementation section only describes argv-based handling; if the env-var is not already mapped to forked_target the documentation update would be factually wrong.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan's step-7a.md update states the new behavior activates when '--forked-target true or LARCH_FORKED_TARGET=true'. Read step-7a.sh to determine whether LARCH_FORKED_TARGET is already parsed and mapped to the forked_target shell variable before the argv loop, or whether the env-var pathway is absent and the documentation claim is inaccurate. Check whether generate-code-flow-diagram.sh or its companion .md update in the plan also surfaces the LARCH_FORKED_TARGET env-var pathway, and flag any asymmetry that would mislead operators who configure via environment rather than argv. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: fork-generator-callsite-test
archetypes.rationale: In the fork skip-mode test the classifier fires before the generator runs, so --base-remote upstream never appears in calls.log; the plan only adds a non-fork green-case assertion, leaving the fork-mode generator invocation path completely untested against regression.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan adds a diagram-skip-forked case where the small/non-runtime classifier fires and the generator is never called, meaning no test ever captures --base-remote upstream in calls.log for a fork. The augmented green case assertion only validates --base-remote origin for non-fork mode. Identify whether test-step-7a.sh includes or the plan adds any case where forked_target=true and the diff exceeds the two-file cap so the generator is actually invoked with --base-remote upstream, and explicitly flag if that call-path is absent from the harness entirely. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
